items.title: Reddit Sinks 6% as Traffic Falls 13% on Google’s AI Overviews: “Not Traffic Drivers”
items.summary: Key TakeawaysReddit shares fell 6% after Similarweb data showed a 13% drop in global visits, which Business Insider blamed on Google’s AI Overviews. Most of the lost visits were logged out, and the logged-in users behind over 80% of its monetization are still growing.

items.title: My parents are in their early 60s with no savings, a mortgage, and $2,400 in Social Security: where can they afford to live?
items.summary: A Reddit poster recently asked for advice about his parents, who have almost no savings and are struggling to cover basic bills. He wants to know where they can afford to live and which steps could build some financial security despite their limited assets.

items.title: I’m 44 with $1.3 million in my 401(k) — can I stop contributing and still retire in 15 years?
items.summary: A Reddit user recently posed an intriguing question: at what point does contributing to a 401(k) become unnecessary because compound growth alone will handle the heavy lifting? The 44-year-old poster has already accumulated $1.3 million and plans to retire at 59 1/2. He noted that even maxing out his contributions would represent just 1% of his account’s expected annual growth. His goal is straightforward: generate at least $100,000 per year in retirement income.
